items.q: Who do I ask for help?
items.a: Knock on the door at the technicians' office. If nobody answers, message a technician on Teams (preferred) or email them. Names are on the Contact page.

items.q: Can I eat or drink in the lab?
items.a: No. No food or drink in the lab.

items.q: A tool is missing from my bench toolbox.
items.a: Check the box against the toolbox list, then report what is missing.

items.q: Can I take equipment out of the lab?
items.a: TODO: confirm the loan policy for instruments and tools.

items.q: Where do I get parts and lab supplies?
items.a: Ask the technicians in the technicians' office. TODO: confirm whether there is a parts request process or a stock list.

items.q: How do I get my poster printed?
items.a: Email the final PDF and its dimensions to the poster printing address. It is free for capstone trifold posters and is usually ready in the technicians' office within 2 days. The poster page writes the email for you.

items.q: Can I run the PCB mill myself?
items.a: No. Only lab technicians operate the LPKF mill. Send them your files; the PCB page has a checker for them.

items.q: Can the mill make plated through-holes or vias?
items.a: No. Connect top and bottom layers by threading a wire through a hole or around the board edge.

items.q: Can I print with PETG or another filament?
items.a: No. Only PLA is allowed on the lab printers.

items.q: Can I watch my 3D print from somewhere else?
items.a: Yes. Each printer has a video stream you can open in VLC on the campus network. See 3D printing.

items.q: My scope reads 10 times too high or too low.
items.a: The probe's 1x/10x switch and the channel's probe setting do not match. Set both to the same value. See the oscilloscope page.

items.q: My function generator puts out twice the voltage I set.
items.a: It is set for a 50 ohm load but driving a high-impedance input. Set the load to High Z. See the function generator page.

items.q: My multimeter reads zero on the current setting.
items.a: The fuse is probably blown, usually from measuring across a source in current mode. Use another meter and report it.

items.q: My power supply shows CC and the voltage dropped.
items.a: Your circuit is drawing the full current limit. Turn the output off and look for a short or a part in backwards before raising the limit.

items.q: My circuit worked yesterday and does not work today.
items.a: Work through the debugging checklist, starting with power and ground.

items.q: This site will not load from home.
items.a: It is only reachable on the campus network. Connect the Northeastern GlobalProtect VPN first. See Remote access.
